subject.title: Feature request: Mid-stream message injection (soft steer)

question: Should OpenClaw keep default steering as boundary-based behavior, or add an explicit soft-steer lifecycle that interrupts or pauses active generation/tool work, injects user input, and resumes with partial context?
rationale: The choice affects shared runtime semantics, channel behavior, session state, provider/runtime compatibility, and whether a new queue mode or command surface should exist.

options.title: Design Opt-In Soft Steer
options.body: Add a separate explicit mode or command for pause-or-abort, inject, and resume semantics with tests for partial output, tool calls, backend rejection, fallback, and upgrade behavior.

options.title: Keep Boundary Steering
options.body: Document current steer semantics as the supported default and limit active fixes to making messages reach the existing boundary-based policy.

options.title: Broaden Default Steer
options.body: Make default steer use the stronger soft-steer lifecycle only after maintainer-approved compatibility proof across channels and runtimes.

recommendation.title: Design Opt-In Soft Steer
recommendation.body: Add a separate explicit mode or command for pause-or-abort, inject, and resume semantics with tests for partial output, tool calls, backend rejection, fallback, and upgrade behavior.

likelyOwner.reason: They authored the prior replacement PR for active non-streaming steering and are the strongest available owner signal for this active-run lifecycle decision.
